Classify HOGs by clique conservation pattern

Source: R/cliques.R
classify_cliques.Rd

Convenience wrapper that runs find_cliques() internally (once for all species, once per top-level clade) and applies a sequential waterfall classification. For fine-grained control over the clique detection parameters per step, call find_cliques() directly.

Usage

classify_cliques(edges, ...)

# Default S3 method
classify_cliques(
  edges,
  target_species,
  clades,
  min_species = 2L,
  stability = NULL,
  min_power = 0.8,
  ...
)

Arguments

edges

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, species1, species2, hog, q_value, effect_size, and type. Must contain ALL edges (conserved + ns + diverged), not pre-filtered, because the differentiated check needs to verify absence of cross-group conserved edges. An optional power column (from find_coexpressologs()) enables the "underpowered" class; without it, or where it is NA, the classification is unchanged.

...

Additional arguments passed to the default method.

target_species

Character vector of all species.

clades

Named list of species vectors, one per clade. Clades may nest but must not cross. A species in no clade forms its own clade. A flat trait is split(names(trait), trait). A tree gives [clades_from_tree()](phy).

min_species

Minimum species for a partial or within-group clique (default 2).

stability

Optional output of clique_stability().

min_power

Detection power below which a non-conserved edge is read as uninformative rather than as evidence against conservation (default 0.8). Only used when edges has power. For rank-test edges (find_coexpressologs(method = "rank")) use 0.9: under the default reference rank p0 their power is at least 0.5 by construction (0 when a direction of the species pair has no call under pval_combine = "max", or neither has under "min"), and it overstates detection.

Value

A data frame with one row per HOG:

hog

HOG identifier

classification

One of "complete", "partial", "differentiated", "trait_specific", "unclassified"

underpowered

TRUE where a differentiated or trait_specific call rests on an edge whose power is below min_power. The classification is kept; this qualifies it. FALSE for every other tier and whenever edges carries no power column.

n_species

Species count in the best clique (NA for unclassified)

best_mean_q

Mean q-value of the best clique (NA for unclassified)

trait_groups

Comma-separated top-level clades that hold the cliques (NA for complete/partial/unclassified)

clade

For trait_specific, the home clade of the cliques. For differentiated, the smallest clade that holds all home clades. Otherwise, the smallest clade that holds the reported clique. NA when no clade holds them, and for unclassified HOGs.

stability_class

From stability results (NA if not provided)

robust

Logical: stability class is at least 0 (NA if no stability results provided)

Details

Each HOG is assigned to exactly one category; earlier categories take precedence.

The pipeline:

  1. complete: all target species form a clique (all C(N,2) edges conserved).

  2. partial: a clique with min_species to N-1 species lies in no clade.

  3. differentiated: cliques sit in two or more disjoint clades, and no conserved edge joins two top-level clades.

  4. trait_specific: all cliques sit in one clade.

  5. unclassified: none of the above.

The home clade of a clique is the smallest clade that holds all its species. A HOG keeps the home clades that no other of its home clades holds. Clades are laminar, so these are disjoint. Nested homes count as one clade, so they are not differentiated. Cliques are searched within each top-level clade. A species in no clade forms its own clade.

Underpowered calls

differentiated and trait_specific both rest on edges that were not conserved. An edge too weak to have been called is no evidence either way, so such a call has to survive reading that edge as conserved. Where it does not, the row is flagged underpowered = TRUE and keeps its classification – the call is reported and qualified, not replaced, so nothing is lost and a caller can filter on it. Needs a power column in edges; without one, or where it is NA, the flag is FALSE.

What the flag marks: power is computed against the typical fold enrichment of a called pair (rho0, about 2.5 on the Pooideae data), and at that enrichment a low-degree gene's shared partners amount to less than one, which no count test can call. So underpowered marks genes whose neighbourhoods are too small for ordinary conservation to be visible – on the Pooideae data most of the lowest degree decile and none of the highest.

Choosing between the two clique classifiers

This function and classify_gene_cliques() answer different questions; neither is deprecated in favour of the other.

classify_cliques() works on the per-orthogroup species graph. It asks which species are joined by conserved co-expression and whether that pattern respects the trait split, and it returns one row per HOG. find_cliques() commits to one best gene assignment per species clique, so a multi-copy HOG still gets a single answer, and that answer is what clique_stability() and clique_threshold_sweep() consume – the stability_class / robust columns exist only on this side.

classify_gene_cliques() works on the gene graph built by gene_clique_graph(). It asks which individual gene copies are mutually conserved, so one HOG can yield several overlapping cliques and the answer names paralogs rather than species. It applies the taxonomy of Rodriguez et al. (2026), plus trait_specific, with two explicit tolerance tiers (partial_significant for weak wiring, partial_present for a missing gene).

Reach for classify_gene_cliques() when which copy sits in the conserved core matters, or when the published taxonomy is what has to be reported. Reach for classify_cliques() for a one-row-per-HOG trait summary wired into the stability machinery.

References

Rodriguez E, Birkeland S, Chapple ED, et al. (2026). Comparative regulomics of wood formation across dicot and conifer trees. Nature Communications 17(1). doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75624-2

See also

find_cliques() for the species-graph backend this wraps; classify_gene_cliques() and gene_clique_graph() for the copy-level alternative described above.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
clades <- list(annual = c("SP_A", "SP_B"), perennial = c("SP_C", "SP_D"))
result <- classify_cliques(edges, target_species, clades)
table(result$classification)
} # }
